title: PJM Capacity Auction Procures 138,318 MW of Generation Resources as Work Continues to Address Growing Electricity Demand
date_evidence: (Valley Forge, PA – July 14, 2026) – PJM Interconnection today announced the results of its 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction
key_claim: The 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction cleared at the FERC-approved cap, procured only 525 MW UCAP of new generation and uprates, and left committed supply 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement.
frame_summary: PJM is arguing that demand is outrunning supply and that the auction alone cannot close the gap, which is why it is layering administrative interventions on top of the market clearing price.
verbatim_quote: The capacity of the resources procured in the auction, plus FRR resources, is short of PJM's reliability requirement by 6,831 MW, meaning that the committed supply is less than what would be required to meet the one-event-in-10-year reliability standard.
verbatim_list: The auction cleared 525 MW UCAP of new generation and generation uprates.
PJM Capacity Auction Procures 138,318 MW of Generation Resources as Work Continues to Address Growing Electricity Demand
notes: The market-failure premise on which the ownership filings rest. Article headline recorded verbatim because the bibliography reproduces it.

title: Over 700 New Generation Projects Accepted into First Cycle of Reformed Interconnection Process
date_evidence: (Valley Forge, PA – Aug. 3, 2026) – PJM Interconnection today announced that 715 new generation projects, capable of generating more than 200 GW of electricity, have qualified to be studied in the first Cycle of PJM's reformed interconnection process.
key_claim: 715 projects capable of more than 200 GW entered the first cycle of PJM's reformed interconnection process, while 51 GW already holding signed agreements are in many cases not being built or are slowed by state permitting and supply-chain backlogs.
frame_summary: PJM is arguing that private developer appetite is strong and its process reform is working, which is the counter-case: the binding constraint is permitting and supply chain rather than who owns the asset.
verbatim_quote: PJM currently has 51 GW of generation with signed agreements, but many of these projects are either not being built at all or are being slowed by hurdles such as state permitting and supply chain backlogs.
notes: Deliberately sourced counter-evidence; used in the Counter-Argument box.

title: Power and utilities: US Deals 2026 midyear outlook
key_claim: Announced US power and utilities M&A totalled $216 billion across 23 transactions in the six months to May 2026, up 173% year on year, with the focus shifting from renewables to dispatchable generation.
frame_summary: PwC is arguing that load growth has opened a new M&A cycle in which regulated balance sheets, not merchant risk capital, become the preferred vehicle for owning dispatchable generation.
verbatim_quote: Over the six months ended May 2026, announced power and utilities M&A activity totaled $216 billion1 across 23 transactions, up 173% from $79 billion across 23 transactions in the prior comparable period ended May 2025.
verbatim_list: The era of renewable generation as the key driver of M&A activity is waning, with the focus shifting to dispatchable generation to meet load demands.
notes: Establishes that capital is moving toward regulated ownership of dispatchable plant.

title: Power and renewables 2026 outlook: half time
key_claim: Aggregate organic investment across leading utilities is set to rise by more than 10% in 2026, with utilities doubling down on network investment and flexible generation while oil and gas majors retreat from power.
frame_summary: Wood Mackenzie is arguing that regulated utilities have become the sector's dominant capital allocators, which is the balance-sheet precondition that makes re-integration financially attractive.
verbatim_quote: Aggregate organic investment across leading utilities is set to rise by more than 10% this year, with networks at the core.
verbatim_list: Utilities are doubling down on network investment and flexible generation, while oil and gas majors continue to retreat from renewable power.
notes: Supplies the capital-allocation context for the Implications section.

title: Right Diagnosis, Wrong Prescription: CRA's Case for Utility-Owned Generation
key_claim: The Charles River Associates analysis commissioned by Exelon models additional utility-owned capacity in PJM, but nothing in the analysis turns on who owns the plants; seeking regulated cost recovery instead of building at shareholder risk shifts investment risk to captive ratepayers.
frame_summary: R Street is arguing that the utility-ownership push is a risk-transfer play rather than a supply solution, because cost-of-service treatment does not make a plant easier to build.
verbatim_quote: The policy change for which Exelon is advocating would shift billions in investment risk from utility shareholders to captive ratepayers.
verbatim_list: Nothing prevents Exelon from forming a new competitive generation subsidiary and building at shareholder risk right now, so seeking regulated cost recovery instead shows they find the downside risks too high.
notes: Structural anchor: the only institutional analysis engaging the ownership question on the merits, and the canonical statement of the counter-case.

title: Exelon 'high probability' data center load falls 40%
key_claim: Atlantic City Electric proposed on 23 July to build and own a 500-MW four-hour battery with Invenergy at a 9.6% ROE, contending this does not breach New Jersey's bar on utility generation ownership, while BGE and Pepco have 150 MW of storage before the Maryland commission.
frame_summary: Utility Dive is reporting that Exelon is pressing utility-owned generation across its restructured jurisdictions on the explicit ground that the capacity market has failed to attract supply at the capped price.
verbatim_quote: In an effort to address some of those challenges in PJM, ACE, working with Invenergy, on July 23 proposed building and owning a 500-MW, four-hour battery storage system in Pittsgrove, New Jersey.
verbatim_list: ACE contends that owning the storage project wouldn't violate New Jersey's restructuring laws for utilities, which bar them from owning generation.
ACE is seeking a 9.6% ROE for the project, with the potential for a higher return if the project meets performance benchmarks, according to its application.
The projects under review by the Maryland Public Service Commission total 150 MW, according to Exelon.
“Even at the highest allowed price, the market is not attracting the level of new supply the system needs,” Calvin Butler, Exelon president and CEO, said during the earnings call.
Exelon’s “high probability” data center load fell nearly 40%, to about 11 GW, in the second quarter from 18 GW at the end of last year, the Chicago-based utility company said Thursday.
notes: Carries the New Jersey and Maryland filings and the Exelon CEO's statement of the market-failure premise.

title: Ohio bill would let utilities own nuclear plants, drawing manufacturer opposition
key_claim: Ohio House Bill 862, introduced in May 2026, would let AEP, FirstEnergy and other Ohio utilities own nuclear plants with construction-work-in-progress recovery and rate-base treatment in a state that generally bars utility generation ownership.
frame_summary: Utility Dive is reporting, through the Ohio Manufacturers' Association, that the bill is being read as a generation-ownership strategy presented as a nuclear strategy.
verbatim_quote: American Electric Power, FirstEnergy and other electric utility companies could own nuclear power plants in Ohio — a state that generally bars utilities from owning generation — under a bill introduced earlier this month in the Ohio House.
verbatim_list: “This bill is not a nuclear development strategy. It is a utility ownership strategy,” Ryan Augsburger, OMA president, said in a press release.
notes: The legislative leg of the signal, and evidence that it is contested rather than settled.

title: PPL-Blackstone joint venture secures 5 GW of gas turbines for data centers in Pennsylvania
key_claim: PPL holds a 51% stake in Invitium Energy, a non-utility joint venture with Blackstone Infrastructure that has reserved turbines representing up to $15 billion of potential investment through 2032, while Pennsylvania legislation permitting utility generation ownership is on the backburner.
frame_summary: Utility Dive is reporting that bilateral contracting through a majority-owned non-utility affiliate, rather than the capacity auction or new legislation, is how a restructured-state utility holding company is rebuilding a generation portfolio.
verbatim_quote: The secured turbines represent up to $15 billion in potential investment through 2032, Sorgi noted. PPL has a 51% stake in the non-utility joint venture.
verbatim_list: PPL-Blackstone joint venture secures 5 GW of gas turbines for data centers in Pennsylvania
Meanwhile, consideration of legislation that would allow utilities in Pennsylvania to own generation appears to be on the backburner, according to Sorgi.
notes: The affiliate route. The 5 GW figure is the article's own headline, recorded verbatim.
